title: 12,700 US Tech Workers Returned to India in Nine Months, Nearing Record
excerpt: Xpheno data shows returns climbing for a fourth year as visa uncertainty and US layoffs rise — but returnees face pay at a quarter to a third of US levels.
body:
• About 12,700 white-collar tech workers returned from the US to India between January and September 2026, already close to the full-year record of 15,100 set in 2025, according to Xpheno data reported by ET.
  • Returns have risen each year — 7,200 in 2023 and 9,800 in 2024 — while outbound movement to the US was 14,500 in the same nine months, so the gap is narrowing but has not closed.
  • Returnees typically face pay at 25% to 33% of US earnings: a US full-stack engineer averages about $105,000, versus $20,000 to $32,000 for comparable top-tier roles in India.
  • If you are weighing a return, recruiters say specialist AI, machine learning, data, cloud and cybersecurity skills — not overseas experience alone — now decide offers.

India is close to a crossover in technology talent movement with the United States. Between January and September 2026, about 12,700 white-collar technology professionals returned to India from the US, according to staffing firm Xpheno data reported by The Economic Times and carried by NewsPoint / The Times of India. Xpheno co-founder Kamal Karanth said the flow is on track to exceed last year's total by year-end.

A four-year climb

The series shows a steady acceleration, not a one-off spike. Xpheno counted 7,200 returnees in 2023, 9,800 in 2024, and 15,100 in all of 2025. The 2026 nine-month figure has already reached 84% of that record. The data covers white-collar technology workers moving in either direction between India and the US, drawn from Xpheno's candidate database, recruitment system and job boards — it is not a count of H-1B visa holders alone.

https://x.com/ZackEiseman/status/2110288718854545879

Outbound movement still leads, at nearly 14,500 professionals moving from India to the US through September. Karanth said the recent H-1B changes could accelerate the shift enough for returnees to outnumber those leaving. Experts linked the trend to uncertainty over US immigration rules and tightening visa regulations over several years, alongside sustained layoffs at large US technology companies over the past two to three years.

The salary reset

Returning is not a lateral move on pay. Experts cited in the report said many returnees settle for 25% to 33% of their US earnings, depending on role, employer, location and project experience. Xpheno put a US H-1B full-stack engineer's average at $105,000 a year, typically ranging from $70,000 to $150,000. Comparable professionals in India, even among the top 1%, earn $20,000 to $32,000.

Whalesbook's summary of the same data makes the same point: Indian employers are holding compensation to domestic structures rather than matching overseas packages for overseas experience alone. TeamLease Digital chief executive Neeti Sharma said applied AI professionals in India can earn roughly Rs 16 lakh to Rs 35 lakh a year, with senior specialists commanding more.

A selective home market

The harder surprise is hiring itself. Karanth said the Indian technology sector has not regained stable hiring momentum since the 2021 surge, with no period of stability lasting beyond a quarter since then, and described the current market as not the best of times for US returnees. Sharma said employers have become more selective, prioritising specialised skills and relevant experience over an overseas stamp.

Demand is strongest, both accounts agree, in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data, product leadership, cloud computing, cybersecurity and enterprise AI implementation. Global capability centres are a real route in, but returnees compete there against experienced candidates already in the domestic pool.

What to watch

The year-end Xpheno total will show whether 2026 sets a record and whether returns overtake departures for the first time in this series. For professionals still in the US weighing the decision now, the numbers argue for negotiating from a specialist skill base and pricing the move at Indian market rates — roughly one-quarter to one-third of US pay — before resigning, not after arriving.
